name: Ouroboros Actuarial Field Sling Pack
description:
Single-strap sling bag in slate-grey ballistic nylon with a narrow Ouroboros snake-circle logo heat-pressed near the top zip. Clean, professional geometry — no exterior pockets, no visible hardware beyond matte gunmetal buckles. The interior is organized obsessively: document sleeves, a rigid tablet compartment, a water-resistant inner lining, and a flat zip pouch for field equipment.

The strap is wide and padded, engineered to clear shoulder-mounted chrome without pinching. A secondary chest clip keeps it stable during rapid movement between sites. Used throughout Tier 3 by claims processors and field investigators who move between corporate campus zones.
functionality: Document sleeves accommodate legal-size forms and flexible displays. Tablet compartment is shock-padded. Strap design routes cleanly over standard shoulder chrome and spinal rig hardware. Chest clip stabilizes load during fast transit between sites. RFID-blocking inner pocket protects client data chips.
what_it_says: This person is organized, mobile, mid-level, and working too many sites to afford a desk.
story_hooks: An investigator's RFID-blocking pocket is holding a data chip that doesn't belong to any case in their active file — and they don't remember putting it there.
The bag is standard-issue at Ouroboros, meaning every field investigator carries the same one — useful if you need to swap bags at a transit hub without anyone noticing.
The rigid tablet compartment has a secondary false panel that the manufacturer has never acknowledged publicly.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist sling pack worn cross-body with a professional geometric silhouette. The narrow Ouroboros serpent logo creates a subtle focal point near the top zip. When worn, it sits compactly against the torso without bulk or external clutter—pure function dressed as form.
physical_description.fit: Worn as a cross-body sling with the bag body resting at mid-hip. The wide, padded strap distributes weight evenly across the shoulder and chest. Secondary chest clip keeps it locked to the body during movement. Designed to clear shoulder-mounted chrome augmentations without catching or pinching.
physical_description.primary_material: Slate-grey ballistic nylon — a dense, abrasion-resistant synthetic with a subtle matte finish
physical_description.texture: Smooth, tightly woven ballistic surface with a professional tactile quality. Interior features a soft, water-resistant technical lining that muffles contents. Strap padding has a subtle ribbed texture for grip.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate grey dominates, with matte gunmetal hardware providing minimal contrast. The Ouroboros logo is heat-pressed in a darker grey-black, nearly disappearing into the fabric at certain angles.
physical_description.closures: Primary top zip with matte gunmetal slider. Secondary chest clip (friction-fit magnetic snap). All closures engineered for one-handed operation.
distinctive_features: Ouroboros snake-circle logo heat-pressed near top zip — subtle corporate marker
Zero exterior pockets — clean geometric profile
Wide, padded shoulder strap with chrome-clearance engineering
Secondary chest clip for stability during rapid movement
Internal document sleeves, rigid tablet compartment, water-resistant lining
Flat zip pouch for field equipment
Matte gunmetal hardware only — no visible branding or excess detail
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional — professional-grade but not luxury. Signals competence and corpo-adjacent legitimacy without ostentatious wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Claims processors, field investigators, insurance auditors, corporate compliance personnel. Wearing this marks you as someone who moves between secured corporate zones and field sites. Trustworthy, methodical, slightly corporate but still street-adjacent.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. Ballistic nylon develops a subtle sheen with use. Zippers show light wear. Interior remains pristine due to obsessive organization habits of its typical users.
